neighbours.label: negating prefix (in-/un-) opening the last adjective of a list of qualities
fire: She was described by her colleagues as patient, thorough and unflappable under pressure.
The new bridge is meant to be light, durable and indestructible in storms.
He wanted his soldiers to look brave, loyal and invincible to the enemy.
We try to keep the classroom warm, welcoming and unhurried for the younger pupils.
The judge seemed calm, fair and incorruptible throughout the trial.
Their marketing called the phone sleek, fast and unbreakable in daily use.
The old captain remained steady, watchful and imperturbable during the gale.
Critics found the novel clever, moving and unputdownable from the first page.
quiet: She was described by her colleagues as patient, thorough and cheerful under pressure.
The new bridge is meant to be light, durable and handsome in all seasons.
He wanted his soldiers to look brave, loyal and confident to the enemy.
We try to keep the classroom warm, welcoming and quiet for the younger pupils.
The judge seemed calm, fair and attentive throughout the trial.
Their marketing called the phone sleek, fast and reliable in daily use.
The old captain remained steady, watchful and silent during the gale.
Critics found the novel clever, moving and gripping from the first page.

notes: card: in-/un-/не- prefixes after 'and' in coordinated praise lists; no probing (time).
